items.title: Yu-Gi-Oh x Crocs Collaboration Revealed Ahead of World Championship
items.description: Crocs and Konami have revealed a new line of clogs inspired by the Yu-Gi-Oh trading card game and anime series.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Crocs and Konami have revealed a new line of clogs inspired by the Yu-Gi-Oh trading card game and anime series.

The collaboration was shown off in a display case ahead of this year's Yu-Gi-Oh World Championship in Tokyo. The line will seemingly include four new pairs of Crocs, two standard and two in the Echo style, each of which is themed after specific characters and cards. Those attending the World Championship also got a look at a new limited-edition Yu-Gi-Oh card themed after the collection.

The Crocs website has a section dedicated to the collaboration, but individual listings have yet to appear. Konami and Crocs have yet to confirm a wide release date or pricing, but some outlets are reporting a potential release in September.

OFFICIAL LOOK: Yu-Gi-Oh! x Crocs Collection 🃏🐉

Classic Clogs
- Yugi Yami
- Seto Kaiba

Echo Clogs
- Dark Magician
- Blue-Eyes White Dragon

🗓️ September 2026 pic.twitter.com/iB9HWKqofE

— Sole Retriever (@SoleRetriever) August 25, 2026

The four Crocs shown off at the World Championship can be seen above. The two standard Clogs are themed after Yugi Mutou, the show’s main character, and his rival Seto Kaiba. The colorways are largely inspired by their respective outfits, Decks, and, of course, Yugi’s iconic hair.

The Echo clogs have quite a bit more dimension, and are both themed after specific cards that also make appearances in the original anime. One pair takes its purple inspiration from the Dark Magician. The other is inspired by none other than the legendary Blue-Eyes White Dragon, Seto’s go-to creature and one of the most valuable cards in real life.

Promotional images also suggest the collaboration will feature a line of Jibbitz, including accessories modeled after straight-up Yu-Gi-Oh cards.

Yu-Gi-Oh really committed to the Crocs collab 😭🐊

Alongside four character-inspired Crocs, they made a “Crocodile” promo card featuring an actual crocodile WEARING Crocs 😂

It’s even Level 3 with 1300 ATK/DEF and flavor text referencing the 13 holes on its feet. pic.twitter.com/49qErCc2Tm

— The Collectibles Guru (@gurucollects) August 25, 2026

Speaking of cards, the Crocs-themed card that was shown off at the convention is simply titled ‘Crocodile,’ a Reptile/Normal card with 1300 ATK and 1300 DEF. Fun fact: Crocs have exactly 13 holes in them. Images posted online don’t appear to show any special card effects, but it could be an interesting grab for collectors.

At this point, there’s no word on whether the card will be available for purchase or included as part of the Crocs collection.

Crocs has truly been going full LEGO mode with the collaborations, including Animal Crossing, Super Mario, and over the next couple of months, Pokemon-themed clogs. They’re not the only shoes looking to franchises, either - a Pokemon x Adidas collaboration is dropping in early September, while Nike just revealed a new One Piece collection.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

items.title: Rockstar Games Doubled in Size for GTA 6, Hired Real World Professionals for Fashion, Vehicles, and More
items.description: Rockstar Games doubled its employee headcount for Grand Theft Auto 6 and hired real-world professionals for the game's vehicles, fashion, and more.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rockstar Games doubled its employee headcount for Grand Theft Auto 6 and hired real-world professionals for the game's vehicles, fashion, and more.

As part of a cover story for Dazed, Rockstar Games shared a boatload of information about Grand Theft Auto 6. In the piece, it was confirmed that Rockstar doubled in size following the release of Red Dead Redemption 2 in order to bring GTA 6 to life, with a new Los Angeles-based office being "almost solely" dedicated to working on nothing but the game's NPCs. For context, Rockstar had around 2,000 employees in 2018. That would put them at around 4,000 now. The studio has expanded a lot over the last decade by acquiring new studios in Australia, India, and the aforementioned LA office.

Rockstar's expansion doesn't exclusively encompass game developers. The company brought on other real-world professionals, such as Miami-based stylist Jillian Carr, who was hired to help create a “fashion ecosystem” that can capture the diversity in style, culture, and class necessary to give Vice City's people their distinct character.

“Vice City is built around vanity,” Carr said to the magazine. “Between social media, celebrity culture and a constant flow of tourists, appearances carry significant weight, and trend cycles turn over quickly.”

Rockstar also hired racecar drivers to help with vehicle handling and 50 real street artists to design murals around the game's map. While consultants are hardly unique to this project, Carr and others are full-time employees at Rockstar and have been for years. Carr was specifically hired in 2023 and appears to be as much of the team's regular operations as anyone else.

Rockstar also revealed new gameplay details for GTA 6, such as how eating, working out, and sleeping all impact your characters and much, much more. It's just the start of a larger bombardment of GTA 6 information, too. Rockstar will officially pull the veil off the game tomorrow in an extended look on Netflix, which is widely expected to give us a deep dive on gameplay.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Gets Pending Mature 17+ Rating, and Fan Theories Are Already Going Wild
items.description: Final Fantasy VII Revelation is available to wishlist on all major platforms, and fans have noticed that its pending rating is a bit more intense than they expected.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Final Fantasy VII Revelation is available to wishlist on all major platforms, and fans have noticed that its pending rating on the Xbox store is a bit more intense than they expected.

Set to release in Spring 2027, the last entry in the Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy wraps up the saga for Cloud and company in their quest to protect the planet from the incoming Meteor.

We’ve gotten a few glimpses at gameplay over the last few months, showing off submarine combat, traversal via the Highwind, and an explanation of the new FITS system — but none of these point to a Mature rating.

That’s the current predicted rating that’s listed on the game’s Xbox page, which says, “Rating pending, likely Mature 17+.” As clarified by the ESRB’s rating system, the Mature rating is given to games that may contain “intense violence, blood and gore, sexual content and/or strong language.”

For now, the game’s rating is still pending, and the Mature prediction is simply a placeholder implemented by the ESRB likely based on many publicly unknown factors prior to its official rating. But why would Revelation be rated Mature, when the first two games in the trilogy were rated T for Teen?

There’s a couple possible explanations for this. The first could be that the ESRB is using the placeholder out of an abundance of caution due to Final Fantasy XVI, which was notably rated Mature due to its sexual themes, language, and overall violence.

The other explanation is that there could be a lot more violence, language, and sexual themes in this particular game… and that possibility is sending fans into a tizzy.

Most can’t help but bring up that saucy scene between Clive and Jill in FF16, wondering if the famous "Highwind scene" between Cloud and Tifa might get a bit more heated than was originally portrayed in the 1997 game.

“I BEG YOUR FINEST PARDON?” one fan wrote on X. “Mature 17+?! Spicy Highwind scene confirmed??? Hello?!”

I BEG YOUR FINEST PARDON

Mature 17+?!

Spicy Highwind scene confirmed????
Hello?! pic.twitter.com/qVJJ4aHjMB

— ✨🌙✨ (@TifaTheMonk) August 26, 2026

“FFVII Revelation may go M rated? This would make it the second mainline game to do so, and I welcome it,” another said. “I want Final Fantasy to embrace that mature rating to explore their heavy, more darker themes with a grace and gravitas that gets muddied by having to compromise.”

FFVII Revelation may go M rated? This would make it the second mainline game to do so and I welcome it.

I want Final Fantasy to embrace that mature rating to explore their heavy, more darker themes with a grace and gravitas that gets muddied by having to compromise.

FFXVI was… pic.twitter.com/QJMuJqRsoy

— Limitless (@MoreLimitless) August 26, 2026

For now, it’s anyone’s guess as to whether or not this pending rating will actually stick. In the meantime, you can check out the most recent reveals for the game, which were shown off at Gamescom’s Opening Night Live showcase along with several other significant gaming announcements.

items.title: Apple iPhone Event Invites Have Gone Out, and I Want a Foldable iPhone
items.description: There are a few things that are inevitable every year, and one of those is that Apple is going to host a big, flashy event in September to show off its new iPhone. And now, Apple has announced a September 9 event that'll do just that.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
There are a few things that are inevitable every year, and one of those things is Apple hosting a big, flashy event in September to show off its newest iPhone. And now, Apple has announced a September 9 event that'll do just that.

The event will happen September 9 at 10am PST, and while the company hasn't shared exactly what's in store, it's not hard to guess that this is where all the latest iPhones are going to get showcased. As for which iPhones will be getting a refresh, its anyone's guess, but it's safe to assume that the iPhone 18 and its Pro version will be there, along with the latest Apple Watch.

But rumors have circled for ages that Apple has been toying with the idea of launching a foldable phone. It feels like this is something that I've been hearing for years now, but with how far foldables have come in the last two years, specifically, this could be the year that Apple finally brings its version to the masses – after all, it has named this iteration of the event "Surprise and Shine." A foldable iPhone would certainly be surprising, to say the least.

Back in July, Apple analyst Ming-Chi Quo predicted that the foldable iPhone would be coming sometime this year, but that it would be in limited supply, with "7–8 million units, with 3Q26 shipments at 0.5–1 million units, or about 10% of the total." He also predicted that if the foldable is real, it'd be quite expensive. That shouldn't be surprising, though, with the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra costing $2,100 when it launched last month.

While that would mean Apple would be quite late to the foldable game, the company has a track record of taking technologies and launching them into the stratosphere. It's hard to imagine that a $2,000 phone is going to have mainstream success, but if any company could do it, it'd be Apple.

Beyond the rumored foldable, though, I don't suspect that the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro are going to be that different from the iPhone 17. The 17 Pro brought a new chassis, with a much better camera shelf, and I'd expect Apple to ride that chassis out for another year.

Whichever iPhones Apple elects to launch this year will probably come with a modest price bump, though. The RAM crisis does apply to phones, and the company has already raised prices on the rest of its product lineup. It wouldn't be surprising, then, that the new iPhone is going to have at least some price increase baked in. At least that would help the company avoid raising prices on older products.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: Fans Mourn Tim Curry After Legendary Actor Dies at 80 Years Old
items.description: Prolific British actor Tim Curry has died aged 80, leaving behind a storied legacy that includes iconic roles in productions like The Rocky Horror Picture Show, Muppet Treasure Island, Home Alone 2, and many more.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Prolific British actor Tim Curry has died aged 80, leaving behind a storied legacy that includes iconic roles in productions like The Rocky Horror Picture Show, Muppet Treasure Island, Home Alone 2, and many more.

News of Curry’s death was announced on August 26, 2026 by his long-term manager and friend Marcia Hurwitz, who confirmed the star died at his home in Toluca Lake, Los Angeles.

Curry suffered a severe stroke in 2012 that left him wheelchair bound, causing lasting issues in his left leg. The actor opened up about the incident in an interview with CBS in October 2025, revealing that the stroke had even impacted his ability to speak.

“I had to learn how to speak again,” he explained. “That was very weird. I hated not being able to speak because I speak a lot. I have to be told to shut up a lot. I love words, I love to communicate.”

Despite his physical limitations as a result of the stroke, Curry continued to work, notably returning to Rocky Horror for the 2016 televised remake of the musical as the story’s narrator, The Criminologist.

Curry was born on April 19, 1946 in Grappenhall, Cheshire. He graduated from the University of Birmingham with a BA in English and drama in 1968. That same year, he joined the original cast of the musical Hair in London, a project that would lead him to meet actor and playwright Richard O’Brien, who famously penned his role as Dr Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Show.

Curry’s performance in the musical, which came to film in 1975, skyrocketed the actor to fame, kicking off the heyday of his career in the 90s and 2000s. Millennials will remember him best as the cagey hotel concierge from Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, Long John Silver in Muppet Treasure Island, and Pennywise the Clown in the 1990 miniseries adaptation of Steven King’s IT.

Curry also boasted a swath of famous voice acting roles, having lent his talents to animated films like FernGully: The Last Rainforest, The Wild Thornberries Movie, and the English dub of Studio Ghibli’s The Cat Returns.

Curry’s last major role in a live-action film was playing Alexander Monro in the 2010 British comedy Burke & Hare. He notably made an appearance at a September 2025 screening of The Rocky Horror Picture Show for the film’s 50th anniversary, where he shared more details about his stroke.

“I was having a massage at the time and I didn’t even actually notice anything, but the guy who was doing the massage said, ‘I’m worried about you, I want to call an ambulance.’ And he did, and I said, ‘That’s so silly.’ I still can’t walk, which is why I’m in this silly chair, and that’s very limiting. So I won’t be singing and I won’t be dancing very soon. I still have real problems with my left leg,” the actor shared.

As noted by The Hollywood Reporter, Curry answered that he wasn’t afraid of dying in response to a question during his October 2025 interview with CBS. “No, I’m not. I don’t fear death. I try to avoid it, as I think we all do, but I suspect that in the end I will welcome it,” he said.

The entertainment world is mourning the loss of two legends in just as many days, with country music legend Dolly Parton's death being announced by her nephew yesterday, August 25.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have RPG Mechanics Like Eating, Exercising, and More
items.description: Some of the first gameplay details for Grand Theft Auto 6 have been confirmed, and it seems like Rockstar is embracing a more RPG-y style this time around.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Some of the first gameplay details for Grand Theft Auto 6 have been confirmed, and it seems like Rockstar is embracing a more RPG-type style this time around.

As part of a cover story for Dazed magazine, Rockstar Games revealed heaps of new information about Grand Theft Auto 6. Arguably the most notable details revolve around some of its gameplay features. In GTA 6, players will be able to eat, work out, and sleep, all of which have an impact on the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia. Players will have to take care of the Bonnie and Clyde-esque couple, as eating will affect their weight, working out will visibly change their build and strength, and a lack of sleep will negatively impact their features. It's unclear if a lack of sleep will impact the actual gameplay, or if they'll just look sleep-deprived, but it's a clear sign of Rockstar's attention to detail.

For many, this may remind them of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. That game featured a lot of RPG mechanics that allowed CJ to fluctuate in weight and fitness. Later games largely dropped these elements, but GTA 5 featured a stat system that allowed players to enhance their stamina and strength by doing physical activities such as running, playing sports, and riding bikes.

Additionally, there is also a social media feed for players to scroll, something fans have speculated about since the game's reveal in 2023. Character switching is also returning from GTA 5, allowing players to play as a couple or split up and operate independently. items.title: The Division 2: Echoes of Central Park Announced
items.description: Massive Entertainment, developers of Tom Clancy's The Division 2, announced a new DLC for the long-running online action-RPG/third-person shooter at a community panel at Gamescom. The new expansion is called Echoes of Central Park, and a full reveal will happen on September 24.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Massive Entertainment, developers of Tom Clancy's The Division 2, announced a new DLC for the long-running online action-RPG/third-person shooter at a community panel at Gamescom. The new expansion is called Echoes of Central Park, and a full reveal will happen on September 24.

The Manhattan-set live-service game will finally head into Central Park due to a distress call from inside it. Echoes promises a darker tone wrapped in fear and mystery, with neither players nor their in-game avatars sure about what's inside or what Central Park has been like since the outbreak.

Massive promises ample replayability for this DLC, including "a few twists" to give gameplay a unique feel. Speaking of gameplay, the developerse also want to lean heavier into gameplay here, rather than just new story content. Exactly how that will manifest itself remains to be seen.

IGN gave The Division 2 an 8.5 out of 10 back in 2019 and the 2020 DLC Warlords of New York an 8 out of 10.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Beta Will Be Playable on Switch 2 for Free This Weekend
items.description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend.

Starting Friday, August 28 at 10 AM PDT, Nintendo Switch 2 players will have the opportunity to try Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for free. The beta's second weekend will kick off, giving Nintendo fans the opportunity to try a level from the game's campaign, multiplayer, and even the battle royale, Warzone.

The Switch 2 version will boast unique features such as gyro controls, Joy-Con mouse controls, and, of course, being able to play the game on a handheld. Additionally, Switch 2 players will get free access to the game's Vault Edition content during the beta. This includes access to special skins, weapon blueprints, and more. Players can pre-load the beta on Switch 2 right now and pre-order the full game.

It's the first time a Call of Duty game has been on a Nintendo platform since Call of Duty: Ghosts on Wii U. Nintendo fans have been wanting to see the franchise return to Nintendo hardware since then, but it hasn't been feasible until now. Digital Legends are developing the game's Switch 2 version after having helped develop Call of Duty: Warzone Mobile before its cancelation. The studio also did support work on the last two Black Ops games.

"For the first time in more than a decade, Call of Duty is back on a Nintendo platform, and we’re incredibly proud that Digital Legends has partnered with Infinity Ward to make it happen with Modern Warfare 4, said Xavier Carrillo-Costa, studio head, Digital Legends. "Our goal has been simple from day one: deliver the genuine Call of Duty experience on Nintendo Switch 2. Players can enjoy the full intensity, authenticity, and quality of Modern Warfare 4 wherever they are, whether at home or on the move."

In 2023, Microsoft signed a legally binding deal with Nintendo to bring Call of Duty games to Nintendo platforms for a decade with full feature parity. That means there's no missing content or notable concessions made to bring Call of Duty to Switch 2. Whether Nintendo fans show up for this release remains to be seen, but it's great to see Switch 2 being supported more and more by the biggest third-party franchises out there.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Leaker Posts Extended Gameplay From GTA 6 Prologue Just Hours After Rockstar Warns Fans to Expect Story Spoilers
items.description: Extended gameplay footage revealing Grand Theft Auto 6's story prologue has been posted online, in a significant escalation of the past week's continued leaks.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Extended gameplay footage revealing Grand Theft Auto 6's story prologue has been posted online, in a significant escalation of the past week's continued leaks.

More than four minutes of gameplay featuring GTA 6 character Lucia is now being spread over social media, in the first lengthy leak of footage that reveals key story details. If you are planning to try and experience GTA 6 with no narrative spoilers, now is the time to beware where you click online over the coming days and weeks.

The footage's release comes just hours after Rockstar finally broke its silence over the leaks, which it called "heartbreaking" for its development team. In its statement, published online earlier today, the developer warned fans that spoilers would likely impact the manner in which it had hoped players would first experience the game — something that now appears to accurate.

A fresh statement from the leaker, included as a watermark in this latest footage, makes several unsubtantiated claims about GTA 6's development, such as the game still being unfinished and that "too much" work remains on the game to be comfortably completed before the title's November 19 release date.

Earlier today, Rockstar noted that it was indeed still working on the game — something that is fully to be expected with nearly three months left to go until launch — but that it was now "nearly" finished. The company also reiterated GTA 6's November 19 launch date, suggesting confidence that nothing would change.

The leaker has also claimed to have a "recent" build of the game, something that is again impossible to verify. However, there is now little doubt that these leaks stem from a polished playable build. Exactly how the leaker has gained access to it remains a mystery, but one which Rockstar and GTA publisher Take-Two are actively taking steps to ascertain.

Finally, the leaker once again called for "support" in the form of their own cryptocurrency, something that has been widely seen as a money-making exercise. Perhaps signalling that their leaking days may be winding down, the leaker suggested that "trading volume/price" of the $Cyberleek currency would determine whether the posting of footage will continue.

The past week has seen more than a dozen gameplay clips appear online, causing significant damage from a Rockstar perspective as numerous sections of GTA 6's world have now been revealed. According to Bloomberg, Rockstar has been left scrambling to discover how these leaks happened and who is behind them, as they have continued now for the past week.

Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, has downplayed the damage caused by the leaks. Vermeij, who worked at Rockstar North from 1995 to 2009, took to social media to say that the company has weathered worse in the past, such as the Hot Coffee scandal.

Of course, all of this is happening with just a day to go until Rockstar Games' own unveiling of GTA 6 gameplay, via its Grand Theft Auto 6 Extended Look. This lengthy and official debut will be released exclusively on Netflix for six hours, before arriving on other platforms such as YouTube. Find out exactly when the GTA 6 Extended Look will be available where you are right here.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Xbox's 25th Anniversary Limited Edition Console Price and Release Date Revealed, Comes With Halo: Campaign Evolved
items.description: Xbox has revealed the price and release date for its 25th anniversary limited edition console, and it comes with a free game too.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Xbox has revealed the price and release date for its 25th anniversary limited edition console, and it comes with a free game too.

Earlier this summer, Microsoft revealed that it will be releasing a translucent green Xbox Series X console, inspired by the original Xbox console, for the company's 25th anniversary. Now, Microsoft has confirmed that the console will cost a whopping $899.99 and release on November 13. It will come with the Xbox Series X console, a matching controller, and a free copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved. Pre-orders will open tomorrow, August 27, at 7 AM PDT.

The controller can be purchased separately for $79.99, and it will release on October 20. If you're in the market for a brand new Xbox, this isn't a bad deal. The Xbox Series X itself costs $799.99 with a disc drive. This costs an extra $100 and includes one of Xbox's biggest games of the year. However, the next-generation of Xbox is also likely right around the corner. Microsoft confirmed earlier this year that it will detail its next console, codenamed Project Helix, later this year.

It wouldn't be surprising if the next Xbox releases in fall 2027, as Microsoft has already indicated that will be a really important window for the company. The company also unveiled plans for a new disc-to-digital feature that will allow users to get a digital copy of their physical Xbox One and Xbox Series X games. It's been speculated that this is to prepare players for a transition to a more digital-focused next-generation console.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Xbox Is Letting Players Digitize Their Physical Games, Starting Next Week for Select Users
items.description: Xbox's new disc-to-digital feature is launching imminently, allowing users to add physical copies of games to their digital library.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Xbox's new disc-to-digital feature is launching imminently, allowing users to add physical copies of games to their digital library.

The new feature will roll out to Xbox Insiders starting on August 31 before making its way to everyone at an unknown future date. This new initiative leaked earlier this summer and will be a way to allow players to put their Xbox One and Xbox Series X discs into their console and get a fully usable digital version.

Your discs will also remain playable, but if you give the game to someone else and they insert that copy into their console, you will lose access to your digital license as well. It's not only great for the sake of convenience, but perhaps more notably, it also enables you to stream the game through the cloud or access it on other devices via Xbox Play Anywhere if the game supports those features.

That means you don't have to have the game installed at all, and you can play it on PC, the ROG Ally, or even your mobile devices. Unfortunately, Microsoft made no mention of this feature being supported with original Xbox or Xbox 360 games, so don't expect those right now. Additionally, not every game will be supported off the bat. However, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the company will support thousands of games when this feature launches, with more added over time. Will that eventually encompass Xbox 360 titles? It's hard to say.

"Your physical game library is more than a collection of discs," said Sharma. "It holds years of memories and stories worth preserving. Starting next week, Xbox Insiders can unlock a digital entitlement for supported physical games. We’ll start with thousands of titles and add more as we can."

Some have speculated that this move is happening to create a smooth transition between this generation and the next Xbox, which may be a digital-only device. Microsoft has yet to confirm such a thing, but given PlayStation won't support discs starting in 2028, physical gaming media may be less of a standard next-gen. Regardless, this is a great feature that will definitely offer a lot of benefits to those who enjoy physical media.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Rupert Grint Returning as Ron Weasley for Harry Potter and The Cursed Child on Broadway
items.description: Harry Potter movie star Rupert Grint will reprise his character of Ron Weasley next year, as he joins the Broadway cast of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Harry Potter movie star Rupert Grint will reprise his character of Ron Weasley next year, as he joins the Broadway cast of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.

Grint is the second Harry Potter movie cast member to return to their childhood role for Cursed Child, the official J.K. Rowling-penned play that picks up the series' story years later, as Harry and Ron's children attend Hogwarts.

Last year, Draco Malfoy actor Tom Felton returned as his fan-favorite Slytherin, supercharging interest in the Broadway production. Now, it seems like the play's producers are keen to pull off the same stunt again, with Grint also the right age to play Ron as a young father.

"Ron Weasley has been a part of me since I was 11 years old and I can't wait to meet him again in this stage of life," Weasley said, via The Hollywood Reporter. "There is something so full-circle and so special about stepping back into Ron's shoes now when we are both fathers; it is somehow both very familiar and completely new. And the joy of being back on Broadway, this time in a role that defined so much of my life is truly exciting."

Grint will begin his stint back as Ron on February 2, 2027, initially for a 17-week run until May 30. However, this does mean his time in the play's company will sadly not overlap with Felton, whose much-extended time in the cast finally ends on January 3, 2027.

While Grint is still best known for his Harry Potter role, the actor has continued to appear in a string of TV and film projects, such as Apple TV horror series Servant, M. Night Shyamalan movie Knock at the Cabin, and this year's upcoming Johnny Depp-starring Ebenezer, in which he plays Bob Cratchit.

"In joining our extraordinary company onstage at the Lyric Theatre in New York City, Rupert is not simply revisiting a role from his past," producers Sonia Friedman and Colin Callender said in a statement. "He is continuing a journey he began as a child and carrying it forward with all the life and experience he has gained since filming concluded, including a career that has taken him from film to television to acclaimed stage work on both Broadway and the West End. His return creates a powerful bridge between the story audiences first fell in love with and the story of family, legacy and the passage of time that Harry Potter and the Cursed Child carries forward."

Of course, a fresh generation of young actors will soon take on the roles of Harry, Ron and Draco in HBO's Harry Potter TV series reboot. Set to launch this Christmas, the show will adapt the franchise over the course of the next decade.

Image credit: Sebastian Reuter/Getty Images

LEGO has unveiled an enormous new Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer set, which will soon become the company's longest model ever.

While not the most expensive LEGO set or the model with the most bricks, the Executor's vast length will break a fresh record for the toy firm in terms of its length. At more than 136 cm long, this 6,130-piece Ultimate Collector Series model is one you'd need a very deep Dagobah swamp to hide in.

Priced at a stonking $799.99 (£649.99), the set will become available on October 4, or via early access to LEGO Insiders from October 1. And if you need to measure up your home to find out if it'll fit, the set's dimensions will be 7.5 inches (20 cm) in height, 53.5 inches (136 cm) in length and 20 inches (50 cm) in width. Finally, it'll weigh just over 11 lbs / 5 kg.

Which ship is the Executor? This is the super sleek, supersized Star Destroyer that Darth Vader uses as his flagship in The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi. Present at the Battle of Hoth and Battle of Endor, this ship is also the setting for Vader's meeting with various bounty hunters, included here as minifigures.

In Star Wars lore, the actual Executor was over 19 km in length — roughly the size of Manhatten. The Executor was only finally beaten when a brave Rebel pilot crashed into its command bridge during the battle around Endor's moon, disabling the gargantuan vessel's shields and sinking it into the second Death Star (another Empire design flaw). It was apparently crewed by a vast army in the hundreds of thousands — but best not think too much about that.

The LEGO Star Wars Executor set will weigh in at a hefty 6,130 pieces and include a mini build of the ship's bridge. Minifigures include Darth Vader, Boba Fett, Dengar, Bossk, IG-88, 4-LOM, and Zuckuss. LEGO Insiders will be eligible for a Gift With Purchase (while stocks last) of a buildable recreation of Darth Vader's Lightsaber.

It's been a busy day for LEGO news, with the full reveal of the company's Super Mario minifigure set range. Keen for something even larger? We have a guide to the biggest LEGO sets you can buy in 2026.

items.title: Exclusive: LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Deluxe Edition - Mayhem Collection DLC Trailer Reveals the Joker and Harley Quinn Story Mission and More
items.description: During our IGN gamescom Studio livestream, we were able to exclusively reveal the LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Deluxe Edition - Mayhem Collection DLC trailer, which features an exciting look at the new story mission starring Harley Quinn and the Joker, the Mayhem Mode, and the Sinister Pack.
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
During the gamescom Studio livestream, IGN exclusively revealed the trailer for LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Deluxe Edition - Mayhem Collection DLC, which features an exciting look at the new story mission starring Harley Quinn and the Joker, the Mayhem Mode, and the Sinister Pack.

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight's Mayhem Collection DLC will be available to all Deluxe Edition owners for no extra cost on September 18, 2026, the same day the game launches on Nintendo Switch 2.

The big addition in the DLC is that new story mission that stars Harley Quinn and The Joker, which will see the pair working together to "orchestrate a breakout from Arkham Asylum with a going-away party Gotham City won't soon forget."

Harley Quinn will be equipped with her trusty hammer and her Fun Gun loaded with Confetti and Bubblegum, and she'll also be able to summon her beloved hyenas, Bud and Lou. As for the Joker, he'll bring his Paintball Pelter and Boxing Glove to the party alongside a "fast-paced, agile combat style that is focused on speed and mobility." Players will also be able to unlock outfits for Harley Quinn and the Joker that are based on past Batman Media, including The Dark Knight Returns comic book series, Batman: The Animated Series, and more.

Outside of the story, the Mayhem Mode will unleash Harley Quinn and the Joker across Gotham City and task them with time-limited Mayhem Runs. During each run, they will need to make it back to Amusement Mile before time runs out, and they will be chased by Batman and Robin while doing so. You'll earn LEGO studs by smashing everything in sight and completing challenges, alongside battling A.R.G.U.S. Agents and members of Amanda Waller's Task Force X in Deathstroke, Killer Croc, Captain Boomerang, Deadshot, King Shark, Polka-Dot Man, and other "notorious DC Super-Villains."

The Sinister Pack includes themed outfits inspired by popular DC comic book issues and action figures, plus a new vehicle and Batcave customization options. The full list of items this pack includes is as follows:

  • Batman – The Batman Who Laughs outfit (Dark Nights: Metal #2 | 2017)
  • Robin – Robin King outfit (Dark Nights: DM – Legends of the Dark Knights #1 | 2020)
  • Nightwing – Joker outfit (Nightwing #16 | 2011)
  • Batgirl – Joker outfit (Jokerized DC Multiverse Action Figure)
  • Jim Gordon – Joker outfit (The Joker: The Man Who Stopped Laughing #9 | 2022)
  • Catwoman – Joker outfit (Catwoman #65 | 1993)
  • Talia al Ghul – Joker (Earth-37) outfit (DC Elseworlds comic series | 1997)
  • Vehicle – Jokermobile (Arkham Trilogy)
  • Batcave Items – Helmet (The Merciless), Joker Fish Aquarium, Barbatos Statue, Snake Clowns, and Long Halloween Pumpkin

The last thing that will be added on September 18 will be an enhanced 'Absolute' difficulty level, which will actually be a free update for all players. This new difficulty mode will require "greater skill, awareness, and precision in combat."

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight released on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC back in May 2026, and in our review, we called it "a strong open-world Gotham and trademark Lego slapstick humour powers a fantastic plastic parody of Batman’s greatest hits."

For more, check out everything announced from Opening Night Live and what else to expect from the rest of gamescom.

Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

items.title: Rockstar Games Finally Addresses Extraordinary and 'Heartbreaking' GTA 6 Leaks, Warns Players That 'Some Spoilers' May Now Impact 'The Intended Game Experience'
items.description: Rockstar Games has finally addressed the past week's extraordinary spate of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Rockstar Games has finally addressed the past week's extraordinary spate of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans.

In a statement posted to social media, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

The past week has seen more than a dozen gameplay clips appear online, posted by an individual or group that has claimed to be leaking material to highlight the death of physical media and the impact this will have on game ownership, while also charging fans to vote on further leaks using cryptocurrency, in what is widely-seen as a money-making exercise.

Today's statement by Rockstar makes no mention of its efforts to try and stop these leaks from occuring, or the legal processes it has begun to try and determine the identity of the leaker(s). Indeed, the statement could be read as an admission that the leaks will likely continue — and worsen, with story spoilers likely — at least in the short term.

As if to confirm this, a 15th clip of GTA 6 has just been posted online, within minutes of Rockstar's statement being made public. It show the leaker driving at night, and then a clip of a cutscene with GTA 6 co-protagonist Lucia. This is particularly noteworthy as the leaker has, so far, only shown off gameplay with the character of Jason, though has suggested that a Lucia story prologue could be leaked in future. Watermarked text includes: "Show support trade $Cyberleek," in reference to the leaker's virtual currency, and "let's get 50m trading volume."

"We know that many of you have been waiting to hear from us regarding the events of the past week," Rockstar Games wrote. "It would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intednd for you to see the game after all this time.

"We are very sorry that everything has taken as long as it has — from getting the game finished (nearly there!) to sharing more details and official gameplay, and providing the community with everything you want to know.

"We are very excited for everyone to see the Extended Look tomorrow," Rockstar continued. "It has taken longer than we wanted to get it ready, but as with everything we do, we know we need to exceed your expetations, and we are determined to deliver at the level you expect and deserve. While it is unfortunate that the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers, we hope that everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19.

"We want to thank everyone in the community who has reached out with messages of support this past week — your words have meant more to this team than you can imagine. Ultimately, we are making this game for you, and without you, we would not have the privilege of making games. We look forward to sharing more with you soon."

From a Take-Two and Rockstar perspective, significant damage is being done as the leaks continue, with numerous sections of the GTA 6's world now revealed. More worrying still, according to Bloomberg, Rockstar still doesn’t know how these leaks happened, nor who is behind them. And while there are no plans to shift this week’s big Netflix reveal, Bloomberg reported that there is frustration and anger internally at recent events, with management sending morale-boosting emails to staff.

Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, downplayed the damage caused by the leaks. Vermeij, who worked at Rockstar North from 1995 to 2009, took to social media to say the Hot Coffee scandal was much more damaging than these GTA 6 leaks.

Rockstar Games will fully reveal GTA 6 gameplay itself later this week via the Grand Theft Auto 6 Extended Look, a lengthy and official debut that will be released exclusively on Netflix for six hours, before arriving on other platforms such as YouTube. Find out exactly when the GTA 6 Extended Look will be available where you are right here.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Marvel Fans Say Avengers: Endgame Encore's Extra 4 Minutes Risk Being 'Really Oversold' After Directors Insist Movie Is 'Required Viewing for Following the Story in Doomsday'
items.description: We all love Avengers: Endgame, but some Marvel fans are now suggesting that the four minutes of footage added to its upcoming Encore re-release risk being oversold by its directors.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
We all love Avengers: Endgame, but some Marvel fans are now suggesting that the four minutes of footage added to its upcoming Encore re-release risk being oversold by its directors.

Endgame is one of the best Marvel movies of all time — perhaps the best — and so it's not surprising to see it return to theaters this fall ahead of Avengers: Doomsday's arrival. Not only will this new chance to watch the film inject a few more million into its box office total (perhaps enough to overtake Avatar once again!), the experience will likely remind cinema audiences of the excitement felt at the close of the Infinity Saga, as a decade of storytelling came to a natural conclusion.

But after the reveal that Avengers: Endgame Encore will be just four minutes longer than the movie's original runtime, fans are revisiting recent comments by directors Joe and Anthony Russo — who suggested that an Endgame watch (or rewatch) was "required viewing" to follow Doomsday's own story — with a healthy dose of scepticism.

A clip of the Russos discussing Avengers: Endgame Encore at San Diego Comic-Con last month is now being shared widely on social media, where the duo discussed why they thought fans should see the film again with Fandango.

"It's going to connect the story of the two movies," Joe Russo said of Avengers: Endgame Encore. "There's a natural progression from Endgame into Doomsday, which is also inclusive of all the other stories that have been playing out.

"But I think it's important to see Endgame in theaters again for two reasons," he continued. "One, if you want to have a lot of fun cheering and screaming and reliving all the emotions you had the first time you saw it. Two, I think it's required viewing for following the story in Doomsday.

"If you saw Endgame when it was originally released, you couldn't see this coming," Anthony Russo added.

Anthony and Joe Russo break down what fans can expect to see in Avengers Endgame: Encore.

Tickets are on sale NOW! Assemble your friends, and get your tickets now👇 https://t.co/CgcsDpHycS pic.twitter.com/AaFAk5c1rf

— Fandango (@Fandango) August 25, 2026

Marvel has not detailed what the new footage added to Avengers: Endgame Encore will comprise, though there's a growing sense among fans that it is likely to be scenes shot during Avengers: Doomsday's production that may also end up within Doomsday itself. Many fans believe this is likely to focus on the journey of Steve Rogers — perhaps showing him returning the Infinity Stones, or returning home to Peggy Carter afterwards, only for his peace and quiet to be swiftly disturbed.

In general, though, there's a sense among fans that Marvel would not actually make Avengers: Doomsday incomprehensible without prior MCU knowledge, and certainly not without actually requiring fans to rewatch a movie that released years ago with a few minutes of extras added on. Doomsday will do very well at the box office regardless, of course, but would hardly benefit if its plot hinged on something that only those who attended a screening of Endgame Encore could understand.

"It's literally four extra minutes of footage that will be in a YouTube short within two days," wrote one Marvel fan, in the top comment of a new and lengthy reddit thread discussing the Russo's claims. "I mean I'm probably still gonna go see it just because Endgame was great, and I'd love to see it again in Dolby, but they are really overselling this extra footage, I think."

"Yeah. Not getting a babysitter," a second fan wrote. "Spending $30-$40 for four minutes of footage. A little tone deaf to say 'required viewing'. I'll wait for the leaks."

"Normal fans aren't going to go shell out $100 for something they can watch for free on Disney+," wrote another fan. "They are going to be unaware there's a few minutes of additional footage. They'll be there for Doomsday though."

"The last thing this world needs is f***ing DLC for movies," added yet another.

"What do you expect them to say?" countered another fan. "'Skip this one guys, it's only 4 extra minutes and you can just watch a recap video on YouTube.' Like of course they're gonna oversell it lol it's their job."

"Am I gonna go see it? Yes," one fan wrote on X/Twitter. "But are you guys false advertising infinity vision and just trying to make more money because it's only [four] minutes, absolutely."

Marvel has currently made no suggestion it will detail exactly what its new Encore footage will contain, likely meaning audiences will find out for themselves when the film's re-release rolls around next month. Will you be going as well? Avengers: Endgame Encore arrives in theaters on September 25 (with Iron Man and Infinity Gauntlet popcorn buckets) before Avengers: Doomsday finally lands on December 18.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Xbox and IKEA Furniture Collaboration Includes Thumbstick Stools, Tables, and D-Pad Accessories
items.description: IKEA has unveiled a range of official Xbox furniture, including gaming chairs, display stands and cozy-looking D-pad cushion.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
IKEA has unveiled a range of official Xbox furniture, including gaming chairs, display stands and cozy-looking D-pad cushions.

The range goes on sale in the U.K. from October via the retailer's website and in IKEA stores, and is officially named "YXSTABY" — a name I won't try and pronounce out loud.

In a press release sent to IGN today, IKEA said that YXSTABY reflected "an era where gaming furniture is moving out of teen bedrooms and man caves and into the mainstream living room."

Created together by Xbox and IKEA designers, the nine-piece collection includes functional furniture such as controller display boxes, TV stands on castors, and a side table to store all your gaming accessories.

There are also more bizarre-looking additions, such as green and black "gaming Thumbstick stools", which really do look like the sticks of an Xbox controller at giant size. IKEA says these were developed using the controller's original 3D design files for maximum authenticity. It even tilts as you lean, echoing the thumbstick's motion to keep gamers "comfortably engaged during intense sessions."

My favorite item is probably the green gaming D-pad cushion, although I do also rather like the D-pad platter, themed after the concave metal D-pad on Xbox Elite pads.

"At Xbox, we think a lot about what helps players feel immersed in a game," said Carl Ledbetter, Xbox Head of Design. items.title: LEGO Super Mario Minifigure Sets Unveiled, Including Bowser's Castle and Mario Kart
items.description: LEGO has finally revealed its Super Mario range that will include minifigures for the first time, including playsets for Bowser's Castle and numerous Mario Kart vehicles.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
LEGO has finally revealed its Super Mario range that will include minifigures for the first time, including playsets for Bowser's Castle and numerous Mario Kart vehicles.

Super Mario has been appearing in LEGO sets for years, though mostly as part of the company's bigger-scale range designed to work with the interactive Super Mario toy unit.

That experiment now seems to over, however, with the long-awaited rollout of Super Mario sets scaled to minifigure size. And indeed, these will also include a growing range of Mario minifigures, with Luigi, Peach, Toad, Yoshi, Koopa Troopa, and Bowser Jr. all glimpsed in this first wave, as well as a Bowser big fig. The range will all be available from January 1, 2027.

LEGO Super Mario Minifigure range

  • Mario's Pipe Jump (72052) – 61 pieces, $9.99
  • Racing with Mario (72054) – 84 pieces, $14.99
  • Mario's Beach Adventures (72055) – 196 pieces, $19.99
  • Luigi & Bowser Jr.'s Race (72056) – 104 pieces, $29.99
  • Yoshi at Mario's House (72057) – 147 pieces, $39.99
  • Bowser's Rumbling Race (72058) – 409 pieces, $59.99
  • Fire Mario & Bowser's Castle (72060) – 850 pieces, $99.99
  • Fire Luigi vs. Koopa Troopa Battle (72061) – 241 pieces, $29.99

The range begins with Mario's Pipe Jump (72052), a 61-piece set priced at $9.99 that features a Mario minifigure, dinky Goomba element and large green warp pipe. Next up is Racing with Mario (72054), an 84-piece set for $14.99 that features a Mario minifigure and the plumber's classic kart. Green and red shells are also included, as is a banana.

Mario's Beach Adventures (72055) sees the hero take some downtime by the sea. This 196-piece set sells for $19.99 and includes a Mario in swim trunks minifigure (no, he doesn't have nipples), plus a buildable snack bar, lounger and giant enemy crab.

Luigi & Bowser Jr.'s Race (72056) is essentially a larger version of the previous Racing with Mario set, except with both Luigi and Bowser Jr. Both characters are included as minifigures, alongside their karts and accessories. This is a 104-piece set that will sell for $29.99.

Moving onto the slightly bigger sets, Yoshi at Mario's House (72057) is a 147-piece build that sells for $39.99. Included here are Mario and a slightly awkward-looking Yoshi minifigure, plus a goomba.

Bowser's Rumbling Race (72058) is another Mario Kart set, this time with 409 pieces for $59.99. Here, you can expand your starting lineup with karts for Toad, Bowser, Goomba and Mario Kart World's fan-favorite Cow. The first two characters are minifigures, while the latter is a buildable design.

The biggest set in this starting wave is Fire Mario & Bowser's Castle, which will weigh in at 850 pieces and sell for $99.99. This features Fire Mario, Peach and Koopa Trooper minifigures, the Bowser big fig and a goomba. It's a cool-looking design, even if LEGO is clearly making us wait for the Peach's Castle set we all really want.

Lastly, Fire Luigi vs. Koopa Troopa Battle (72061) is a smaller 241-piece set featuring, unsurprisingly, Fire Luigi and a Koopa Troopa minifigures.

"The new LEGO minifigures mark a refreshed LEGO Super Mario theme, newly centred on creative LEGO minifigure roleplay action," LEGO stated in a press release today. "The refresh of the Super Mario theme will see building experiences arriving for LEGO Super Mario centred on creative LEGO minifigure roleplay, featuring iconic characters, karts, and environments from the Super Mario and Mario Kart universe."

So, which will you be picking up?

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Atari Is Re-Releasing 39 Atari 2600 Games on Working, Physical Cartridges
items.description: Atari has today announced a new physical game collaboration with Activision called the Atari x Activision Collection, reuniting Activision with Atari after almost 50 years.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
Atari has today announced a new physical game collaboration with Activision called the Atari x Activision Collection. The unexpected project reunites Activision with Atari after almost 50 years.

The full set of working, physical game cartridges includes 39 classic Activision games, like Pitfall!, River Raid, and Kaboom!, and there will be three ways to purchase them.

Individual, “Standard Edition” versions of 12 of the games will be available from November for USD$35 each. The 12 games include Pitfall!, River Raid, Megamania, Enduro, Kaboom!, H.E.R.O., Pressure Cooker, Private Eye, River Raid II, Keystone Kapers, The Activision Decathlon, and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns (although Atari notes The Activision Decathlon and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns will actually ship at a later date than the other titles). The Standard Edition games feature full packaging and a printed, colour manual inspired by the original releases. They’ll be compatible with Atari 2600+ and Atari 7800+ consoles, as well as original Atari 2600 and 7800 hardware.

There will also be four box sets available, which will widen the collection to the full 39 games. The first of the four box sets (which are dubbed Treasure, Speed, Secrets, and Victory) will be available from late November, with the remaining three will follow over the first three quarters of 2027. These will be available via pre-orders at atari.com for USD$250. A complete collection of all 39 games (which will reportedly include a yet-to-be-announced “collectible item”) will also be sold via pre-order for USD$1000.

“In 1979, a group of Atari programmers set out to prove that great games could come from independent creators and ended up changing the industry forever,” said Atari’s VP of hardware Matt Burnett in a comment published in conjunction with today’s announcement. “The Atari x Activision Collection brings that legacy to life through the games themselves, giving fans an opportunity to experience, collect and preserve the work of the developers who helped establish a new model for the video game industry.”

The resurrection of fresh, physical versions of Activision’s very oldest games comes as an interesting surprise amid the bleak times collectors of physical media are currently otherwise facing, and with PlayStation maintaining its decision to discontinue physical discs in the near future won’t have any negative impact on its business either now or in the future.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: Wilderings: The Lost Spring Gameplay Trailer Reveals Volcanic Biome, a Moth Boss, and a Version 1.0 Release Window
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
At gamescom 2026, Kabam and Herobeat Studios revealed a brand-new gameplay trailer for Wilderings that unveiled a fiery new Volcanic biome, a first look at Röhe the Moth Boss, and the confirmation that the open-world action-adventure game will be launching its Version 1.0 update in spring 2027.

Wilderings, which also encourages exploration and features fast-paced action, roguelite progression, and creature collecting, follows Abi and her companion Rif as they traverse a fractured world that is quickly being consumed by darkness.

To help in her journey, she will discover and adopt mysterious creatures known as Hântu, which she can use to help her fight, get through tough spots with their abilities, and to move about the world. In this new Volcanic biome, Abi will run into at least three Hântu, Razzle (explosive projectiles that burn and multiply), Mokul (summons pyroclastic rain that scorches an area), and Furioso (throws magma that spreads between enemies).

As for Röhe, this Moth Boss is actually a young hunter from the Frostlands who will challenge Abi in this new region. To make it through the test set in a "magma-lit arena," Abi will have to perfet her movement, combat skills, and Hântu abilities.

For those at gamescom, Wilderings: The Lost Spring will be available to play at the Indie Arena Booth, Hall 10.2 Booth F010g–E019, from August 26–30.

For more, check out everything announced from Opening Night Live and what else to expect from the rest of gamescom.

Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.
